title: Erdős Problem #294: Egyptian Fractions and the t(N) Function
description: Let t(N) be the least t with no Egyptian representation of 1 using denominators in [t,N]. Estimate t(N).

meta.author: Paul Erdős & Ronald Graham
meta.assumptions: 4 axiom declarations: t_func_exists (t(N) exists for all N), erdos_graham_1980 (upper bound t(N) << N/log N), liu_sawhney_2024 (matching lower bound pinning t(N) up to polylog factors), f_func_exists (f(n) exists for n>=6). Former axioms egyptian_236, t_func_characterization, t_2, t_6_lower, harmonic_asymptotic, almost_all_work, t_f_relationship, greedy_terminates now proved as theorems or definitions.

overview.historicalContext:
**Ancient Origins**

Egyptian fractions date to the Rhind Papyrus (c. 1650 BCE), where ancient Egyptians expressed fractions exclusively as sums of distinct unit fractions. This representation system persisted for millennia and influenced Greek and medieval mathematics.

**The Erdős-Graham Monograph (1980)**

Paul Erdős and Ronald Graham introduced Problem #294 in their influential monograph 'Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory.' They defined t(N) as the smallest starting point from which no Egyptian representation of 1 exists using denominators in [t, N]. They proved t(N) ≪ N/log N but confessed they had 'no idea' of the true asymptotic behavior.

**The 44-Year Wait**

For over four decades, the lower bound remained elusive. The gap between the trivial lower bound and Erdős-Graham's upper bound was enormous—no one knew if t(N) grew like √N, N/log N, or something in between.

**Liu-Sawhney Resolution (2024)**

Yifan Liu and Mehtaab Sawhney finally resolved the problem in 2024, proving t(N) ≫ N/((log N)(log log N)³(log log log N)^O(1)). This matches Erdős-Graham's upper bound up to polylogarithmic factors, settling one of the longest-standing open problems in combinatorial number theory.
overview.problemStatement: Let N ≥ 1 and let t(N) be the least integer t such that there is NO solution to 1 = 1/n₁ + 1/n₂ + ⋯ + 1/nₖ with t = n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ < nₖ ≤ N. Estimate t(N).
overview.text: Let t(N) be the least t with no Egyptian representation of 1 using denominators in [t,N]. Estimate t(N).
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines Egyptian fractions as sums over finite sets and the t(N) function as a minimum over non-representable starting points. The Erdős-Graham upper bound and Liu-Sawhney lower bound are axiomatized. The main theorem confirms t(N) ≍ N/((log N)(log log N)^O(1)).
keyInsights: t(N) measures the 'density' of Egyptian representations of 1
The harmonic sum H_N = ∑1/k ≈ log N plays a key role
Almost all starting points t < N allow representations
The gap between upper and lower bounds is only polylogarithmic

sections.title: Overview, Imports and Namespace
sections.summary: File header: problem statement (t(N) for Egyptian fractions in [t,N]), background, known results (Erdős-Graham 1980, Liu-Sawhney 2024), imports, and the `Erdos294` namespace.

sections.title: Part I: Egyptian Fractions
sections.summary: Defines unitFraction (1/n), egyptianSum, and isEgyptianRepresentationOf1 (a finite set of distinct positive integers whose reciprocals sum to 1).

sections.title: Part II: The t(N) Function
sections.summary: Defines hasConstrainedRepresentation (Egyptian rep of 1 with denominators in [t,N]), axiomatizes existence of a blocking t, and defines t_func via Nat.find.

sections.title: Part III: Small Values
sections.summary: Documents small cases t(2), t(6) via the {2,3,6} representation, and defines the harmonic sum harmonicSum(N) with its log-asymptotic note.

sections.title: Part IV: Erdős-Graham Upper Bound
sections.summary: States erdosGrahamUpperBound (t(N) ≪ N/log N), axiomatizes erdos_graham_1980, and gives the interpretation that few starting points block representations.

sections.title: Part V: The Liu-Sawhney Theorem
sections.summary: States the Liu-Sawhney lower bound (2024), combines it with the upper bound into liuSawhneyTheorem, axiomatizes liu_sawhney_2024, and proves the main theorem erdos_294.

sections.title: Part VI: Implications
sections.summary: States the density interpretation (almost all starting points admit representations) and the harmonic-sum connection relating hasConstrainedRepresentation to partial harmonic sums.

sections.title: Part VII: Related Functions
sections.summary: Introduces the f(n) function (minimum number of distinct unit fractions summing to 1 with largest denominator n), axiomatizes its existence for n ≥ 6, and notes its relationship to t(N).

sections.title: Part VIII: The Greedy Algorithm
sections.summary: Defines greedyStep (smallest n with 1/n ≤ q) and greedyRelation, describing the greedy Egyptian-fraction algorithm and its connection to constrained representations.

sections.title: Part IX: Computational Aspects
sections.summary: Notes that computing t(N) exactly is hard (no known efficient algorithm) and lists small known values via knownValues.

sections.title: Part X: Main Results Summary
sections.summary: Summarizes the resolution (Erdős-Graham upper bound + Liu-Sawhney lower bound), proves erdos_294_summary combining both bounds, and records the SOLVED status.

conclusion.summary: Problem #294 is SOLVED. Erdős-Graham (1980) proved t(N) ≪ N/log N. Liu-Sawhney (2024) proved the matching lower bound t(N) ≫ N/((log N)(log log N)³...), determining t(N) up to polylogarithmic factors.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: The result shows that 'almost all' starting points allow Egyptian representations of 1, with the exceptional set having density ≈ (log N)/N.

This connects to deep questions about harmonic sums and prime distributions.
openQuestions: Can the polylogarithmic gap be closed?
What is the exact value of t(N) for small N?
Is there an efficient algorithm to compute t(N)?
What about Egyptian representations of other rationals?
